questions.question: Which statistic describes how precisely a sample mean estimates the population mean?
questions.explanation: The standard error measures the sampling variability of the mean. The standard deviation describes how spread out individual values are.

questions.question: Collecting more data generally makes the standard deviation of a sample...
questions.explanation: More people do not make individuals more alike, so s stabilises near σ. It is the standard error that keeps shrinking.

questions.question: A sample has n = 49 and s = 14. What is the standard error of the mean?
For the midterm scores 72, 85, 68, 91, 77, 83, 64, 80 (SD ≈ 9.09, n = 8), what is the SE?
You want to cut your SE in half. By what factor must the sample size increase?
questions.explanation: SE ∝ 1/√n. Halving it requires √n to double, so n must quadruple.

questions.question: A pilot study suggests σ ≈ 15. What is the smallest n that gives SE ≤ 1?
